every rib, column, wall and peg added to a part survives the cuts that follow
every printable part is one solid piece with nothing floating (peg gauge: 2 pieces by design)
thinnest plan wall (front corners) 1.29 mm ≥ 1.0
receptacle mouth sits 0.20 mm behind the fascia, for an overmould of any height (USB-C tolerates ≤ 0.5)
port panel 0.8 mm thick, fascia 24.7 mm wide
web between the two port windows 1.96 mm
slim plugs (slim 10.5 × 6.0 mm overmould) in both ports touch no part of any shell
two slim plugs side by side clear each other by 0.90 mm
slim plug top 8.83 mm vs Core top 9 mm
max plugs (largest the USB-C spec allows, 12.35 × 6.5 mm) in both ports touch no part of any shell
two max plugs overlap by 0.95 mm: the board puts its sockets 11.4 mm apart, so this pair cannot share any case. Each fits alone.
max plug top 9.08 mm vs Core top 9 mm: stands 0.08 mm proud, by design of the socket height
blade vents: openings offset 1.79 mm through the lid vs 1.00 mm slot, so there is no straight path down; dust shelf at 40°, under dust's ~45° angle of repose
ribs between the vents 0.71 mm thick measured square to the slope (≥ 0.7 prints as two lines)
side gills climb 1.20 mm through the wall vs 0.8 mm opening, so there is no straight path in
blade field spans x 5.4–22.6 mm, clear of the clamp ribs at 3.6 and 24.3
9 blade vents, 87 mm² open over the shield (31% of its area)
type: 33 marks on 6 faces, all inside their face and clear of every hole, foot and edge; smallest caps 1.60 mm
core: no metal or copper added within 15 mm of the antenna; the shell has no screws
sense: no metal or copper added within 15 mm of the antenna (3 parts, all behind the board's ground plane); the shell has no screws
go: aaa-1 sits 4.5 mm from the antenna, inside Espressif's 15 mm. The cells cannot fit under the board any further forward; expect some loss of range on battery models, and measure it.
antenna has 2.5 mm of air above, 3.0 mm below, 1.0 mm behind before any plastic
top: a 9.8 N press (a firm thumb) closes the 0.2 mm gap; past that the lid rests on the module's steel shield and the USB-C shells, so the board takes the load

pocket: the shell alone carries 214 N pressed across its middle before PETG yields (a hard hand press is 100–200 N); at 100 N it bends 0.43 mm, which the board tolerates. A person sitting on it on an edge (500 N+) can crack it, like most plastic gadgets
1 m drop: the board's 88 N impact load spreads over 115 mm² of rail, 0.77 MPa, far below PETG's 22 MPa across layers

1 m drop, top face down: the plate leaves with 29 mJ; friction over 3.8 mm of peg absorbs it if each peg grips with 3.9 N or more. A snug hand-press fit is roughly 10–20 N (estimate; the peg gauge checks yours)
Go door, top-down 1 m drop: it leaves with 15.7 mJ. Two Ø3 magnet pairs held ~2 mJ (it would open), so the door is now held by a captive nylon M2.5, coin-turned, good for ~237 N
plugging in: 20 N goes into the two rear stops at 1.9 MPa; pulling out: into the port panel at 1.5 MPa. Neither passes through the socket's solder joints
carried weight, with board: Core 20 g, Sense 27 g, Go 53 g with cells
